newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end lower on foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end lower on foreign sales.

text.p: A wave of selling by foreign investors dragged Chilean blue chips down more than one percent at the close, traders said, saying they saw the market remaining soft for the rest of the week.
"There has been heavy selling but without any news which could justify the fall," one dealer said.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 1.08 percent at 94.63 points. The general IGPA index lost 0.6 percent to 5,164.39 pesos.
Volume rose to 13.8 billion pesos, nearly double Monday's turnover, boosted by a 2-billion-peso offering of department store Falabella stock.

Traders attributed part of the slide to a delayed reaction to Chile's ballooning trade deficit, which sparked fears that the central bank will not cut interest rates until well into next year, traders said.
"The speculation is now that the tight credit policy will last until the second quarter of next year," a trader said.
Bank figures showed Chile's trade deficit rising to $487.4 million last month from $128.8 million in the same month 1995.
Dealers reported foreign investors selling Chilean stocks and switching funds into markets with higher growth potential.
Lehman Brothers recently cut Chile's weighting in its investment portfolio to give greater weighting to Mexican stocks.
Decliners included power generator Endesa, on fears of weak fourth quarter earnings after the company said it has to buy expensive electricity from outside producers.
Recent cuts in generating prices also cast a shadow over earnings in the longer term, dealers said.
Endesa ended down 1.95 percent at 238-3/4 pesos. Enersis shed 1.64 percent to 240 pesos.
Advancers included copper mine Mantos, up five percent at 735 pesos, winery Concha y Toro, up 0.78 percent at 193-1/2 pesos and Entel, which rose 0.55 percent to 3,650 pesos.
